claim: Septins are considered as the fourth component of the cytoskeleton.
source: Today septins are considered as the fourth component of the cytoskeleton, with the Septin7 isoform playing a critical role in the formation of higher-order structures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction discussing septins' interactions with other cytoskeletal elements.

claim: Septin7 plays a critical role in the formation of higher-order structures.
source: Today septins are considered as the fourth component of the cytoskeleton, with the Septin7 isoform playing a critical role in the formation of higher-order structures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Septin7 conditional knockdown (KD) mice displayed a characteristic hunchback phenotype with skeletal deformities.
source: KD mice displayed a characteristic hunchback phenotype with skeletal deformities, reduction in in vivo and in vitro force generation, and disorganized mitochondrial networks.
evidence: This is supported by images in Figure 2A and CT imaging data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Septin7 KD mice showed reduction in in vivo and in vitro force generation.
source: KD mice displayed a characteristic hunchback phenotype with skeletal deformities, reduction in in vivo and in vitro force generation, and disorganized mitochondrial networks.
evidence: This is supported by grip force measurements (Figure 2E) and in vitro force measurements (Figure 2F-I).

claim: Septin7 KD mice showed disorganized mitochondrial networks.
source: KD mice displayed a characteristic hunchback phenotype with skeletal deformities, reduction in in vivo and in vitro force generation, and disorganized mitochondrial networks.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5.

claim: Knockout of Septin7 in C2C12 cells resulted in complete loss of cell division.
source: Furthermore, knockout of Septin7 in C2C12 cells resulted in complete loss of cell division while KD cells provided evidence that Septin7 is essential for proper myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by transmitted light images in Figure 3B and 3C showing abnormal cell size and stopped proliferation.

claim: Septin7 is essential for proper myotube differentiation.
source: Furthermore, knockout of Septin7 in C2C12 cells resulted in complete loss of cell division while KD cells provided evidence that Septin7 is essential for proper myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by fusion index data in Figure 3J showing suppressed differentiation in S7-KD cells.

claim: Septin7 expression increases transiently following muscle injury.
source: These and the transient increase in Septin7 expression following muscle injury suggest that it may be involved in muscle regeneration and development.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6C and 6E showing increased Septin7 expression after BaCl2-induced injury.

claim: Septin7 may be involved in muscle regeneration and development.
source: These and the transient increase in Septin7 expression following muscle injury suggest that it may be involved in muscle regeneration and development.
evidence: This is speculative based on the observed increase in Septin7 expression following injury and its correlation with Pax7 expression.

claim: Septins have been first described as regulators of cytokinesis and cell polarity in yeast.
source: Septins have been first described as regulators of cytokinesis and cell polarity in yeast, and since their discovery (Hartwell, 1971) their expression has been demonstrated in many other organisms, including mice and humans.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hartwell, 1971.

claim: Septin expression has been demonstrated in many organisms, including mice and humans.
source: Septins have been first described as regulators of cytokinesis and cell polarity in yeast, and since their discovery (Hartwell, 1971) their expression has been demonstrated in many other organisms, including mice and humans.
evidence: This is supported by the manuscript's own data showing septin expression in human and mouse skeletal muscle (Figure 1A, 1B).

claim: Septins are involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Septins are involved in cell mobility.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kelley et al., 2015.

claim: Septins are involved in apoptosis.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2016 and Fung et al., 2014.

claim: Septins are involved in endocytosis.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hall and Russell, 2012 and Barve et al., 2018.

claim: Septins are involved in determining cell shape.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mostowy et al., 2011.

claim: Septins are involved in mechano-transductional pathways.
source: Numerous studies imply the important role of septins in several intracellular processes as molecular scaffolds and diffusion barriers that control localization of membrane proteins. They are also involved in host–pathogen interactions during infections, in cell mobility (Kelley et al., 2015), apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2016; Fung et al., 2014), endocytosis (Hall and Russell, 2012; Barve et al., 2018), determining cell shape (Mostowy et al., 2011), and even in mechano-transductional pathways (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caudron and Barral, 2009; Gladfelter et al., 2001; Lam and Calvo, 2019; Mostowy and Cossart, 2012.

claim: Septins interact with actin, microtubules, and membrane structures of cells.
source: Since septins interact with actin, microtubules, and membrane structures of cells and assemble into filaments, they became generally accepted as the fourth cytoskeletal component (Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mostowy and Cossart, 2012 and by the manuscript's own data showing co-localization of Septin7 with actin (Figure 3A).

claim: Septins assemble into filaments.
source: Since septins interact with actin, microtubules, and membrane structures of cells and assemble into filaments, they became generally accepted as the fourth cytoskeletal component (Mostowy and Cossart, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mostowy and Cossart, 2012 and by the manuscript's own immunofluorescence data showing filamentous structures (Figure 1F, Figure 3A).

claim: Septins are 30–65 kDa highly conserved GTP-binding proteins.
source: It is already known that these 30–65 kDa highly conserved GTP-binding proteins form hetero-oligomeric complexes, and besides filaments, they polymerize into higher-order structures, sheets, rings, and cage-like formations contributing to biological processes (Weirich et al., 2008; Bertin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Septins form hetero-oligomeric complexes.
source: It is already known that these 30–65 kDa highly conserved GTP-binding proteins form hetero-oligomeric complexes, and besides filaments, they polymerize into higher-order structures, sheets, rings, and cage-like formations contributing to biological processes (Weirich et al., 2008; Bertin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weirich et al., 2008 and Bertin et al., 2010.

claim: Septins polymerize into higher-order structures, sheets, rings, and cage-like formations.
source: It is already known that these 30–65 kDa highly conserved GTP-binding proteins form hetero-oligomeric complexes, and besides filaments, they polymerize into higher-order structures, sheets, rings, and cage-like formations contributing to biological processes (Weirich et al., 2008; Bertin et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Weirich et al., 2008 and Bertin et al., 2010.

claim: In humans, 13 different septin isoforms were identified.
source: In humans, 13 different isoforms were identified, which were classified into four groups (SEPTIN 2, 3, 6, and 7) on the basis of sequence homology (Hall et al., 2005), with a lone presence of Septin7 in its group.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hall et al., 2005.

claim: Human septins were classified into four groups (SEPTIN 2, 3, 6, and 7) on the basis of sequence homology.
source: In humans, 13 different isoforms were identified, which were classified into four groups (SEPTIN 2, 3, 6, and 7) on the basis of sequence homology (Hall et al., 2005), with a lone presence of Septin7 in its group.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hall et al., 2005.

claim: Septin7 is the only member in its homology group.
source: In humans, 13 different isoforms were identified, which were classified into four groups (SEPTIN 2, 3, 6, and 7) on the basis of sequence homology (Hall et al., 2005), with a lone presence of Septin7 in its group.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hall et al., 2005.

claim: Septin expression is ubiquitous and/or tissue-specific.
source: Their ubiquitous (Hall et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2007; Connolly et al., 2011) and/or tissue-specific expression influences the localization and function of cell surface proteins (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Spiliotis and Nelson, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hall et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2007; Connolly et al., 2011.

claim: Septin expression influences the localization and function of cell surface proteins.
source: Their ubiquitous (Hall et al., 2005; Cao et al., 2007; Connolly et al., 2011) and/or tissue-specific expression influences the localization and function of cell surface proteins (Caudron and Barral, 2009; Spiliotis and Nelson, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Caudron and Barral, 2009 and Spiliotis and Nelson, 2006.

claim: Altered expression of septins has been linked to neurodegenerative or excretory system diseases, cardiovascular failures, immunological problems, or cancer.
source: The altered expression of septins has been linked to neurodegenerative or excretory system diseases, cardiovascular failures, immunological problems, or cancer (Dolat et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dolat et al., 2014.

claim: Septin filaments are predominantly made up of hexamers and octamers.
source: Septin filaments are predominantly made up of hexamers and octamers of septins belonging to three or all four of homology groups, according to the cell type.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: All septin filaments include Septin7.
source: All of these filaments include the Septin7, which indicates the pivotal role of this ubiquitous protein in the formation of hetero-oligomeric complexes described to date (Sirajuddin et al., 2007; Jiao et al., 2020; DeRose et al., 2020; Soroor et al., 2021; Mendonça et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sirajuddin et al., 2007; Jiao et al., 2020; DeRose et al., 2020; Soroor et al., 2021; Mendonça et al., 2021.

claim: Knockout of Septin7 is embryonic lethal.
source: The knockout of Septin7 is embryonic lethal. Its absence resulted in the loss of other septin proteins in the oligomers (Kinoshita et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kinoshita et al., 2002.

claim: Absence of Septin7 resulted in the loss of other septin proteins in the oligomers.
source: The knockout of Septin7 is embryonic lethal. Its absence resulted in the loss of other septin proteins in the oligomers (Kinoshita et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kinoshita et al., 2002.

claim: Septin7 has been proposed as a novel regulator of neuronal Ca2+ homeostasis.
source: Furthermore, Septin7 has been proposed as a novel regulator of neuronal Ca2+ homoeostasis (Deb and Hasan, 2016; Deb et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deb and Hasan, 2016 and Deb et al., 2016.

claim: Septin7 downregulates the expression of Orai and inositol-trisphosphate-receptor 3 (IP3R).
source: It has been revealed to downregulate the expression of the Orai and inositol-trisphosphate-receptor 3 (IP3R), subsequently affecting the cytosolic Ca2+ by which it can cause deficient flight ability in Drosophila melanogaster (Deb et al., 2016; Tada et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Deb et al., 2016 and Tada et al., 2007.

claim: Knockdown of Septin7 resulted in myofibrillar disorganization and functionally reduced ventricular contractility and cardiac output in Zebrafish.
source: Knockdown of Septin7 resulted in myofibrillar disorganization and functionally reduced ventricular contractility and cardiac output in Zebrafish (Dash et al., 2017), caused an alteration of myosin heavy-chain localization and disorganization of muscle fibers in somatic muscle (Dash et al., 2017), and significantly affected cytoskeleton dynamics in the ophthalmic artery (Perumal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dash et al., 2017.

claim: Knockdown of Septin7 caused an alteration of myosin heavy-chain localization and disorganization of muscle fibers in somatic muscle.
source: Knockdown of Septin7 resulted in myofibrillar disorganization and functionally reduced ventricular contractility and cardiac output in Zebrafish (Dash et al., 2017), caused an alteration of myosin heavy-chain localization and disorganization of muscle fibers in somatic muscle (Dash et al., 2017), and significantly affected cytoskeleton dynamics in the ophthalmic artery (Perumal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Dash et al., 2017.

claim: Knockdown of Septin7 significantly affected cytoskeleton dynamics in the ophthalmic artery.
source: Knockdown of Septin7 resulted in myofibrillar disorganization and functionally reduced ventricular contractility and cardiac output in Zebrafish (Dash et al., 2017), caused an alteration of myosin heavy-chain localization and disorganization of muscle fibers in somatic muscle (Dash et al., 2017), and significantly affected cytoskeleton dynamics in the ophthalmic artery (Perumal et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Perumal et al., 2020.

claim: mRNA expression of representative members from all homology groups of septins has been detected in human skeletal muscle.
source: mRNA expression of representative members from all homology groups of septins has been detected in total lysates of human skeletal muscle by RT-PCR reactions on m. quadriceps femoris from amputated limbs (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Most septin isoforms have been confirmed at the mRNA level in skeletal muscles originating from neonatal (4-day-old) C57BL/6J mice.
source: Most of the septin isoforms have been confirmed at the mRNA level in skeletal muscles originating from neonatal (4-day-old) C57BL/6J mice, as well.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The expression pattern of septins was similar in muscles of adult mice (4-month-old), although some isoforms (Septin5-Septin10) showed decreased intensity.
source: The expression pattern was similar in muscles of adult mice (4-month-old), although some of the isoforms (Septin5-Septin10) showed decreased intensity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1B comparing neonatal and adult mouse muscle.

claim: A differentiation-dependent expression pattern of septins was revealed in C2C12 cells.
source: In parallel to the age-related alteration in mRNA expression of certain septin isoforms, a differentiation-dependent expression pattern of septins was revealed in C2C12 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Septin1 and Septin3 were barely expressed in C2C12 cells.
source: Septin1 and Septin3 were barely expressed, Septin4 and Septin7 expression showed gradual increase, while signals for other isoforms were rather uniform at different time points.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Septin4 and Septin7 expression showed gradual increase during C2C12 differentiation.
source: Septin1 and Septin3 were barely expressed, Septin4 and Septin7 expression showed gradual increase, while signals for other isoforms were rather uniform at different time points.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Septin12 and Septin14 were not detectable in C2C12 cells.
source: Septin12 and Septin14 – similarly to human and mouse muscle – were not detectable.
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Septin7 protein expression declined gradually with age in mouse skeletal muscle.
source: Septin7 protein expression declined gradually with age, as evidenced by comparing muscle samples from 4-week-old and 4-month-old mice to newborns.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: Septin7 expression is independent of muscle type.
source: On the other hand, Septin7 expression seems to be independent of muscle type since signals were similar in different types of muscles (m. tibialis anterior – TA, m. extensor digitorum longus – EDL, and m. soleus – Sol) at the selected time points (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C and 1D comparing different muscle types.

claim: Septin7 is located next to the Z-line similarly to α-actinin in skeletal muscle fibers.
source: Data acquired from confocal images showed that Septin7 is located next to the Z-line similarly to α-actinin and Septin7 signals were observed between the terminal cisternae characterized by RyR1 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Septin7 signals were observed between the terminal cisternae characterized by RyR1.
source: Data acquired from confocal images showed that Septin7 is located next to the Z-line similarly to α-actinin and Septin7 signals were observed between the terminal cisternae characterized by RyR1 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E-H.

claim: Partial deletion of Septin7 resulted in a significant decrease of Septin7 protein expression to 59 ± 8% in m. quadriceps and 63 ± 8% in m. pectoralis compared to Cre- mice.
source: Partial deletion resulted in a significant and similar decrease of Septin7 protein expression in both muscle types studied (to 59 ± 8 and 63 ± 8% compared to Cre- mice, in m. quadriceps and m. pectoralis, respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and G)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and 1G.

claim: Approximately 50% deletion of Septin7 was achieved in different skeletal muscle types based on three-primer PCR method of gDNA.
source: which correlated well with the approximately 50% deletion based on the three-primer PCR method of gDNA that was achieved in the different skeletal muscle types (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is supported by PCR data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: A pronounced spinal deformity was manifest in Cre+ mice creating a hunchback.
source: In addition, a pronounced spinal deformity was manifest in Cre+ mice in which the spine curved excessively outward, creating a hunchback (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by images in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The average angle of the 10th thoracic vertebra was significantly smaller in Cre+ animals compared to Cre- littermates.
source: From CT images of three individual Cre+ and Cre- mice, we determined the average angle of the 10th thoracic vertebra (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), and this parameter was significantly smaller in Cre+ animals compared to the Cre- littermates, providing further evidence for the deformity of the vertebra (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by CT imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: Cre+ mice had significantly smaller body weight starting from the age of the seventh week.
source: In line with the visible morphological changes, Cre+ mice had significantly smaller body weight starting from the age of the seventh week (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by body weight data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Tamoxifen treatment alone did not induce spinal deformity.
source: As tamoxifen alone did not induce this deformity, it is likely to be the consequence of muscle atrophy and a weaker muscle tone.
evidence: This is supported by comparison data between BL6 and Cre- mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The spinal deformity is likely the consequence of muscle atrophy and a weaker muscle tone.
source: As tamoxifen alone did not induce this deformity, it is likely to be the consequence of muscle atrophy and a weaker muscle tone.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tamoxifen alone did not cause deformity and the reduced muscle force in Cre+ mice.

claim: No significant difference was found between control BL6 and Cre- mice in terms of phenotype and body weight gain.
source: The effect of tamoxifen treatment can be excluded since no significant difference was found between control BL6 and Cre- mice in terms of phenotype and the body weight gain (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The average grip force normalized to body weight was significantly smaller in Cre+ animals compared to Cre- mice.
source: The average grip force normalized to body weight was similar in control BL6 and Cre- mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), while significantly smaller values were measured in Cre+ animals (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by grip force data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: All parameters of running (distance, duration, average speed, maximal speed) were significantly smaller in Cre+ animals compared to BL6 or Cre- mice.
source: All parameters of running (distance, duration, average speed, maximal speed) were significantly smaller in Cre+ animals compared either to BL6 or Cre- mice, while there was no difference between the parameters of running in BL6 and Cre- mice (Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is supported by voluntary running test data shown in Supplementary file 1b.

claim: Both twitch and tetanic force decreased significantly in EDL and Sol muscle of Cre+ mice compared to Cre- littermates.
source: Both twitch and tetanic force decreased significantly in EDL (Figure 2F–I) and Sol muscle (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H–K) of Cre+ mice alike compared to the same muscles of Cre- littermates.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro force measurement data shown in Figure 2F-I and Figure 2—figure supplement 2H-K.

claim: Tamoxifen treatment alone had no effect on the contractile parameters.
source: This reduction in maximal force was the result of reduced Septin7 content since tamoxifen treatment alone had no effect on the contractile parameters (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–K).
evidence: This is supported by comparison data between BL6 and Cre- mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D-K.

claim: The kinetics of twitches and tetani as well as the fatigability changed only in Sol of Cre+ mice.
source: Interestingly, the kinetics of twitches and tetani as well as the fatigability changed only in Sol of Cre+ mice (Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Supplementary file 1c.

claim: Septin7 fundamentally contributes to the normal skeletal muscle performance.
source: In vivo and in vitro force measurements thus suggest that Septin7 fundamentally contributes to the normal skeletal muscle performance.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced force measurements in Cre+ mice.

claim: Significant alteration of the contractile proteins (actin and myosin) was not detected in Cre+ mice.
source: Significant alteration of the contractile proteins was not detected; in addition, the expression pattern of L-type calcium channel (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C) was also similar when the images of Cre- and Cre+ samples were compared.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A and B.

claim: The expression pattern of L-type calcium channel was similar in Cre- and Cre+ samples.
source: Significant alteration of the contractile proteins was not detected; in addition, the expression pattern of L-type calcium channel (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C) was also similar when the images of Cre- and Cre+ samples were compared.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Septin7 shows filamentous structure and co-localization with actin in proliferating C2C12 myoblasts.
source: In proliferating C2C12 myoblasts, the cellular distribution of Septin7 (green) was detected along with the actin-network (red) using immunocytochemistry (Figure 3A), which revealed filamentous structure of Septin7 and its co-localization with actin.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Complete KO of Septin7 in C2C12 cells prevents appropriate cell proliferation.
source: Transmitted light images of control (B) and Septin7 knockout (KO; C) cells demonstrating that complete KO of Septin7 in C2C12 cells prevents appropriate cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by transmitted light images shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: Partial knockdown of Septin7 expression was achieved in S7-KD cells.
source: Partial knockdown (KD) of Septin7 expression at proliferation stage (nondifferentiated [ND]) and 5 days after differentiation induction (D5).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: S7-KD cells showed altered filament structure, cell size, and shape.
source: Immunolabeling of Septin7 filaments in Scr (E) and S7-KD cells (F) demonstrating altered filament structure, cell size, and shape.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E and 3F.

claim: S7-KD cultures showed significant differences in average cell cross-sectional area and circularity compared to Scr cultures.
source: Changes in cell morphology were further analyzed, and significant differences in average cell cross-sectional area and circularity were found in S7-KD cells compared to Scr cultures (Figure 3G and H).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3G and 3H.

claim: In S7-KD cultures, a specific population of cells was present which were large in size and lost their processes, resulting in a more rounded shape.
source: These data express quantitatively the conspicuous visual observations, that is, in S7-KD cultures a specific population of cells was present, which were large in size and lost their processes, resulting in a more rounded shape.
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3G and 3H and visual observations in Figure 3F.

claim: Control and Scr cells did not show any significant changes in cell area and circularity.
source: At the same time, control and Scr cells did not show any significant changes with respect to these parameters (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E)
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The perimeter of individual cells revealed no significant difference between control, Scr, and KD cultures.
source: while the perimeter of the individual cells revealed no significant difference between control, Scr, and KD cultures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Significantly reduced proliferation was observed in Septin7-modified cells.
source: Myoblast proliferation capacity was also tested and significantly reduced proliferation was observed in Septin7-modified cells (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by CyQUANT proliferation assay data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Only negligible cell fusion was detected in S7-KD cultures, even at the sixth day of the experiment.
source: From the second day of differentiation onward, increasing myotube formation was observed in control and Scr cultures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G), while only negligible cell fusion was detected in S7-KD cultures, even at the sixth day of the experiment (Figure 3J, Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is supported by fusion index data shown in Figure 3J and Figure 3—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Both the average area and the perimeter of myofibrils from Cre+ animals were significantly smaller than the corresponding parameters of myofibrils from Cre- mice.
source: As Figure 4C demonstrates, both the average area and the perimeter of myofibrils from Cre+ animals were significantly smaller than the corresponding parameters of myofibrils from Cre- mice.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The number of myofibrils within a given area of the visual field was increased significantly in samples originating from Cre+ mice compared to sections of Cre- animals.
source: In line with the above, the number of myofibrils within a given area of the visual field (Figure 4D) was increased significantly in samples originating from Cre+ mice compared to sections of Cre- animals.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There was no significant difference between the corresponding parameters of myofibrils isolated from BL6 and Cre- animals.
source: On the other hand, there was no significant difference between the corresponding parameters of myofibrils isolated from BL6 and Cre- animals (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D)
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: The markedly reduced size and increased number of the individual myofibrils per unit area in Cre+ mice are attributable to the modified Septin7 expression in their skeletal muscle.
source: suggesting that the markedly reduced size and increased number of the individual myofibrils per unit area in Cre+ mice are attributable to the modified Septin7 expression in their skeletal muscle.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison between BL6, Cre-, and Cre+ mice showing differences only in Cre+ mice.

claim: The calculated average perimeter and area of mitochondria were significantly increased in Cre+ samples compared to data of muscles from Cre- animals or control BL6 mice.
source: The calculated average perimeter (Figure 5C) and area (Figure 5D, inset) were found to be significantly increased in Cre+ samples compared to data of either muscles from Cre- animals or to the samples of control BL6 mice.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: The relative distribution of the mitochondrial area was slightly altered in Cre+ samples with the appearance of larger mitochondria.
source: The relative distribution of the mitochondrial area was also slightly altered in Cre+ samples (Figure 5D) with the appearance of larger mitochondria
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Aspect ratio (AR) was significantly reduced in Cre+ samples compared to Cre-.
source: AR was significantly reduced in Cre+ samples compared to Cre-, while there was no significant difference in the calculated FF parameters of the two sample groups (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: There was no significant difference in the calculated form factor (FF) parameters between Cre- and Cre+ samples.
source: AR was significantly reduced in Cre+ samples compared to Cre-, while there was no significant difference in the calculated FF parameters of the two sample groups (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The number of mitochondria per unit area within the selected visual fields was significantly increased in samples from Cre+ mice compared with the muscles of Cre- or BL6 mice.
source: The number of mitochondria per unit area within the selected visual fields was also significantly increased in samples from Cre+ mice compared with the muscles of Cre- or BL6 mice, as shown in Figure 5E.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Mitochondria-related parameters were not different between the BL6 control and Cre- groups.
source: Mitochondria-related parameters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D) were not different between the BL6 control and Cre- groups.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: The occurrence of large mitochondrial networks has been identified in most images taken from Cre+ muscles in longitudinal sections.
source: Transmission electron microscopic analysis of longitudinal sections from the different animal groups revealed normal myofibrillar structure (sarcomere length, triad composition) in Cre- samples, while the occurrence of large mitochondrial networks has been identified in most images taken from Cre+ muscles, as demonstrated by representative images in Figure 5F and G, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5F and 5G.

claim: The average area, perimeter, AR, and FF were significantly higher in Cre+ samples compared with the Cre- counterparts in longitudinal sections.
source: Assessing the morphological parameters revealed clear changes in the average area (Figure 5I, inset), perimeter, AR, and FF (Figure 5H) in longitudinal sections. These parameters were significantly higher in Cre+ samples compared with the Cre- counterparts.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5H and 5I.

claim: The relative distribution of mitochondrial area demonstrates the appearance of mitochondria with large areas in Cre+ mice that were not present in Cre- mice.
source: The relative distribution of mitochondrial area demonstrates the appearance of mitochondria with large areas (Figure 5I) that were not present in Cre- mice.
evidence: This is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Mitochondrial DNA content was severely reduced in muscles from Cre+ mice compared to data of Cre- mice in both m. pectoralis and m. quadriceps.
source: Mitochondrial DNA content in different muscles, m. pectoralis and m. quadriceps, was also determined. Mitochondrial (16S) RNA content was found to be severely reduced in muscles from Cre+ mice compared to data of Cre- mice in both examined muscles, respectively (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: Not only mitochondrial morphology but presumably mitochondrial function is also severely affected by the alteration of Septin7 expression in skeletal muscles.
source: These results suggest that not only mitochondrial morphology but presumably mitochondrial function is also severely affected by the alteration of Septin7 expression in skeletal muscles.
evidence: This is inferred from the observed changes in mitochondrial morphology and reduced mitochondrial DNA content.

claim: In Septin7-modified KD cells, not only the filamentous structure of Septin7 was different compared to control and Scr cultures, but the mitochondrial network was also severely affected following the Septin7 gene silencing.
source: In Septin7-modified KD cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C), not only the filamentous structure of Septin7 was different compared to the control (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A) and Scr (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B) cultures, but the mitochondrial network was also severely affected following the Septin7 gene silencing.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Septin7 has a prominent role in muscle development and structural assembly of newborn animals and in proliferating C2C12 cells.
source: Previous data (shown in Figure 1C and D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) suggested that Septin7 has a prominent role in muscle development and structural assembly of newborn animals and in proliferating C2C12 cells, thus changes of its expression during muscle regeneration were analyzed.
evidence: This is inferred from the ontogenesis-dependent expression data shown in Figure 1.

claim: More intensive PAX7-positive signal and regeneration-induced, central nuclei in the myofibrils were detected in injected muscles compared to noninjected controls.
source: More intensive PAX7-positive signal and regeneration-induced, central nuclei in the myofibrils were detected in injected muscles (see magnified region of Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B) in Figure 6B compared to noninjected controls (Figure 6A) using DAB reaction.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A and 6B.

claim: The level of Pax7 expression was significantly higher in the injected than in the noninjected muscles.
source: As demonstrated in Figure 6D and F, the level of Pax7 expression was found to be significantly higher in the injected than in the noninjected muscles.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6D and 6F.

claim: Western blot analysis revealed pronounced overexpression of Septin7 at each time point investigated during regeneration.
source: Septin7 protein expression was also monitored for 2 weeks during regeneration (Figure 6C), and Western blot analysis revealed pronounced overexpression at each time point investigated (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C and 6E.

claim: Similar upregulation of Septin7 and Pax7 detected upon BaCl2-induced muscle injury suggests that cytoplasmic septins potentially contribute to regeneration via regulating proliferation and differentiation of newly formed muscle cells.
source: Similar upregulation of Septin7 and Pax7 detected upon BaCl2-induced muscle injury suggests that cytoplasmic septins potentially contribute to regeneration via regulating proliferation and differentiation of newly formed muscle cells.
evidence: This is speculative based on the correlation between Septin7 and Pax7 expression during regeneration.

claim: The presence of at least one essential member of each homology group indicates the possibility of build-up of the previously described hetero-oligomeric structure.
source: Based on their mRNA expression profile in mouse and human skeletal muscle samples, the presence of at least one essential member of each homology group indicates the possibility of build-up of the previously described hetero-oligomeric structure (Sirajuddin et al., 2007; Jiao et al., 2020; DeRose et al., 2020; Soroor et al., 2021; Mendonça et al., 2021).
evidence: This is inferred from the mRNA expression data and supported by citations.

claim: Genetic deletion of Septin7, Septin9, or Septin11 resulted in embryonic lethality, reflecting their essential role in early, intrauterine development.
source: In line with the observation, that genetic deletion of Septin7, Septin9, or Septin11 resulted in embryonic lethality, reflecting their essential role in early, intrauterine development (Hall et al., 2008; Füchtbauer et al., 2011; Röseler et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hall et al., 2008; Füchtbauer et al., 2011; Röseler et al., 2011.

claim: Septins participate in mechano-transduction by promoting the formation of contractile actomyosin networks, and the recruitment of myosin to actin in cancer-associated fibroblasts, in mammalian epithelial cells, and mouse cardiac epithelial cells.
source: Septins participate in mechano-transduction by promoting the formation of contractile actomyosin networks, and the recruitment of myosin to actin in cancer-associated fibroblasts, in mammalian epithelial cells, and mouse cardiac epithelial cells (see the review Lam and Calvo, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the review by Lam and Calvo, 2019.

claim: Interaction of Septin-2, 6, 7, and 9 with the cytosolic elements has an essential role in the regulation of cardiac functions during embryogenesis.
source: This is in line with the observation that during embryogenesis interaction of Septin-2, 6, 7, and 9 with the cytosolic elements has an essential role in the regulation of cardiac functions (Ahuja et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ahuja et al., 2006.

claim: Downregulation of Septin7 has been implicated in abnormal morphology and immature sperm.
source: Downregulation of the ubiquitous Septin7 has been implicated in several pathological events, including abnormal morphology and immature sperm (Chao et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chao et al., 2010.

claim: Downregulation of Septin7 has been implicated in altered glucose uptake in the insulin-sensitive podocytes.
source: Downregulation of the ubiquitous Septin7 has been implicated in several pathological events, including abnormal morphology and immature sperm (Chao et al., 2010); altered glucose uptake in the insulin-sensitive podocytes (Wasik et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wasik et al., 2012.

claim: Downregulation of Septin7 has been implicated in inefficient microvascular angiogenesis, actomyosin organizations, and directional migration in primary mouse cardiac endothelial cells.
source: Downregulation of the ubiquitous Septin7 has been implicated in several pathological events, including abnormal morphology and immature sperm (Chao et al., 2010); altered glucose uptake in the insulin-sensitive podocytes (Wasik et al., 2012); inefficient microvascular angiogenesis, actomyosin organizations, and directional migration in primary mouse cardiac endothelial cells (Liu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liu et al., 2014.

claim: In resting neurons suppressed dSeptin7 resulted in Ca2+ store-independent opening of Orai, a calcium release-activated calcium channel.
source: Septin7 has been suggested as a novel regulator of neuronal calcium homeostasis since in resting neurons suppressed dSeptin7 (homologue of human SEPTIN7 in Drosophila) resulted in Ca2+ store-independent opening of Orai, a calcium release-activated calcium channel (Deb et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Deb et al., 2016.

claim: Septin7 deficiency alters the morphology of mature neurons.
source: Also, Septin7 deficiency alters the morphology of mature neurons (Tada et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2007; Cho et al., 2011; Yadav et al., 2017), leading to neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and neuropsychiatric lupus erythematosus.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tada et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2007; Cho et al., 2011; Yadav et al., 2017.

claim: Septin7 deficiency leads to neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and neuropsychiatric lupus erythematosus.
source: Also, Septin7 deficiency alters the morphology of mature neurons (Tada et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2007; Cho et al., 2011; Yadav et al., 2017), leading to neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, schizophrenia, and neuropsychiatric lupus erythematosus.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Tada et al., 2007; Xie et al., 2007; Cho et al., 2011; Yadav et al., 2017.

claim: The earliest possible application of tamoxifen, administering it to pregnant Cre- females, resulted in stillborn offspring.
source: Unfortunately, the earliest possible application of tamoxifen, that is, administering it to pregnant Cre- females, resulted in stillborn offspring.
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported in the manuscript.

claim: Short applications of tamoxifen, 1 month or less, in young or adult animals resulted in only a minor (<20%) reduction in Septin7 expression with inconclusive modifications in muscle function.
source: Short applications, 1 month or less, in young or adult animals resulted in only a minor (<20%) reduction in Septin7 expression with inconclusive modifications in muscle function.
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported in the manuscript.

claim: Three-month-long tamoxifen treatment gave appreciable (~50%) reduction at the protein level and definite changes in function.
source: These trials led us to use longer (3-month-long, as described) tamoxifen treatment, which gave appreciable (~50%) reduction at the protein level and definite changes in function.
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported in the manuscript.

claim: It was not tamoxifen feeding alone rather the consequent reduction in Septin7 expression that was responsible for the alterations seen in Cre+ mice.
source: These experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1) confirmed that it was not tamoxifen feeding alone rather the consequent reduction in Septin7 expression that was responsible for the alterations seen in Cre+ mice.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison experiments between tamoxifen-treated Cre- and BL6 control mice.

claim: The muscle atrophy and decreased muscle tone observed in Cre+ animals are assumed to be responsible for the vertebral defect.
source: The muscle atrophy and decreased muscle tone observed in Cre+ animals are assumed to be responsible for this vertebral defect since tamoxifen treatment alone did not cause similar malformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that tamoxifen alone did not cause deformity.

claim: Tamoxifen had effects on muscle structure or body weight when administered to mice with impaired muscle function.
source: It should be noted, however, that such effects of tamoxifen were administered to mice with impaired muscle function, that is, to mdx mice (mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy) (Dorchies et al., 2013), to FKRPP448L mutant mice with dystroglycanopathy (Wu et al., 2018), and to Mtm1 knockout mice (murine model of myotubular myopathy) (Maani et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Dorchies et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2018; Maani et al., 2018.

claim: Septins are essential regulators of cell division from yeast to Drosophila.
source: This is in line with previous observations that septins are essential regulators of cell division from yeast to Drosophila (Kim et al., 2011; McMurray et al., 2011; Oegema et al., 2000; Joo et al., 2007; El Amine et al., 2013; Kechad et al., 2012) and in CHO cells (Oh and Bi, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2011; McMurray et al., 2011; Oegema et al., 2000; Joo et al., 2007; El Amine et al., 2013; Kechad et al., 2012; Oh and Bi, 2011.

claim: In epithelial cells, septin filaments are involved in chromosome movement and spindle elongation during mitosis.
source: In epithelial cells, septin filaments are involved in chromosome movement and spindle elongation during mitosis (Spiliotis et al., 2005; Zhu et al., 2008), and even cytokinesis of T cells requires the presence of septins (Mostowy and Cossart, 2012; Mujal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Spiliotis et al., 2005 and Zhu et al., 2008.

claim: Cytokinesis of T cells requires the presence of septins.
source: In epithelial cells, septin filaments are involved in chromosome movement and spindle elongation during mitosis (Spiliotis et al., 2005; Zhu et al., 2008), and even cytokinesis of T cells requires the presence of septins (Mostowy and Cossart, 2012; Mujal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mostowy and Cossart, 2012 and Mujal et al., 2016.

claim: Septin7 determines cell morphology in different cell types, like dorsal root ganglia neurons in the nervous system.
source: This correlates with the observation that Septin7 determines cell morphology in different cell types, like dorsal root ganglia neurons in the nervous system (Boubakar et al., 2017; Ageta-Ishihara et al., 2013), or in mouse primary fibroblasts (Menon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Boubakar et al., 2017 and Ageta-Ishihara et al., 2013.

claim: Septin7 determines cell morphology in mouse primary fibroblasts.
source: This correlates with the observation that Septin7 determines cell morphology in different cell types, like dorsal root ganglia neurons in the nervous system (Boubakar et al., 2017; Ageta-Ishihara et al., 2013), or in mouse primary fibroblasts (Menon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Menon et al., 2014.

claim: Involvement of Septin7 as a target gene of miR-127-3p has been revealed in the regulation of C2C12 proliferation.
source: Finally, involvement of Septin7 as a target gene of miR-127-3p has been revealed in the regulation of C2C12 proliferation (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Li et al., 2020.

claim: Cytoskeletal septin organization has a pivotal role in determining cell morphology, proliferation, and differentiation of skeletal muscle cells.
source: These observations, together with our data, suggest that cytoskeletal septin organization has a pivotal role in determining cell morphology, proliferation, and differentiation of skeletal muscle cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the manuscript's own data and previous literature.

claim: Altered cell morphology and filopodia formation in KD cultures imply the potential role of Septin7 in myoblast migration.
source: Furthermore, altered cell morphology and filopodia formation in KD cultures also imply the potential role of Septin7 in myoblast migration.
evidence: This is speculative based on observed morphological changes.

claim: Modifying the expression of specific septin isoforms (in some cases Septin7) alters the migration of different eukaryotic cell types.
source: Some publications already discussed that modifying the expression of specific septin isoforms (in some cases Septin7) alters the migration of different eukaryotic cell types, like microvascular endothelial cells (Liu et al., 2014), human epithelial cells (Sun et al., 2019), neural crest cells (Boubakar et al., 2017), and human breast cancer or lung cancer cells (Zhang et al., 2016; Zeng et al., 2019; Elkhadragy et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2014; Sun et al., 2019; Boubakar et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2016; Zeng et al., 2019; Elkhadragy et al., 2020.

claim: The cytoskeleton has been shown to alter mitochondrial movement and distribution in highly polarized cells and play a role in mitochondrial dynamics.
source: The cytoskeleton has been shown to alter mitochondrial movement and distribution in highly polarized cells and play a role in mitochondrial dynamics (see the review Pagliuso et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the review by Pagliuso et al., 2018.

claim: In septin-depleted cells elongated mitochondria were developed due to decreased fission rather than to a defective mitochondrial fusion.
source: In particular, in septin-depleted cells elongated mitochondria were developed due to decreased fission rather than to a defective mitochondrial fusion (Pagliuso et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pagliuso et al., 2016.

claim: Depletion of Septin-2 has been shown to influence mitochondrial morphology in HeLa cells.
source: Depletion of Septin-2 has been shown to influence mitochondrial morphology in HeLa cells (Pagliuso et al., 2016), and in Caenorhabditis elegans (Pagliuso et al., 2016), suggesting that the role of septins in mitochondrial dynamics is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pagliuso et al., 2016.

claim: Depletion of Septin-2 has been shown to influence mitochondrial morphology in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Depletion of Septin-2 has been shown to influence mitochondrial morphology in HeLa cells (Pagliuso et al., 2016), and in Caenorhabditis elegans (Pagliuso et al., 2016), suggesting that the role of septins in mitochondrial dynamics is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pagliuso et al., 2016.

claim: The role of septins in mitochondrial dynamics is evolutionarily conserved.
source: Depletion of Septin-2 has been shown to influence mitochondrial morphology in HeLa cells (Pagliuso et al., 2016), and in Caenorhabditis elegans (Pagliuso et al., 2016), suggesting that the role of septins in mitochondrial dynamics is evolutionarily conserved.
evidence: This is inferred from observations across different species.

claim: Septin7 co-localization with mitochondria was shown to affect the proliferation of Shigella flexneri.
source: The contribution of mitochondria-associated septin cages is also described; for example, Septin7 co-localization with mitochondria was shown to affect the proliferation of Shigella flexneri (Sirianni et al., 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sirianni et al., 2016.

claim: Disrupted mitochondrial morphology was detected in the ciliate Tetrahymena thermophila following modification of septin expression.
source: while disrupted mitochondrial morphology was detected in the ciliate Tetrahymena thermophila following modification of septin expression (Wloga et al., 2008), suggesting that septins maintain mitochondrial stability in ciliates and free-living protists.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wloga et al., 2008.

claim: Septins maintain mitochondrial stability in ciliates and free-living protists.
source: while disrupted mitochondrial morphology was detected in the ciliate Tetrahymena thermophila following modification of septin expression (Wloga et al., 2008), suggesting that septins maintain mitochondrial stability in ciliates and free-living protists.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation in Tetrahymena thermophila.

claim: Septin7 could play an important role in muscle regeneration.
source: Measurements on cultured C2C12 cells suggested that Septin7 is involved in myogenic cell division and myoblast fusion. This in turn indicated, based on previous experiments on satellite cells (see the review Wang and Rudnicki, 2011), that it could play an important role in muscle regeneration, too.
evidence: This is inferred from C2C12 cell data and supported by citation to Wang and Rudnicki, 2011.

claim: Septin7 expression is increased following a mild muscle injury induced by the injection of BaCl2.
source: Indeed, we found (Figure 6C and E) that Septin7 expression is increased following a mild muscle injury induced by the injection of BaCl2.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C and 6E.

claim: The most intense regeneration was seen a few days after the injury, while after 2 weeks regeneration was essentially complete and the expression of Pax7 and Septin7 returned to baseline.
source: In line with previous observations (Seale et al., 2000; Sambasivan et al., 2011), the most intense regeneration, and thus the increase in the expression of both Pax7 and Septin7, was seen a few days after the injury, while after 2 weeks regeneration was essentially complete and the expression of the two molecules returned to baseline.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C-F and citations to Seale et al., 2000 and Sambasivan et al., 2011.

claim: The appearances of Pax7 as well as that of centrally located nuclei are accepted markers of muscle regeneration.
source: As the appearances of Pax7 as well as that of centrally located nuclei are accepted markers of muscle regeneration (Lepper et al., 2011; Mazzotti and Coletti, 2016), we concluded that the increased expression of Septin7 could also be an essential component of the regeneration process.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lepper et al., 2011 and Mazzotti and Coletti, 2016.

claim: The increased expression of Septin7 could be an essential component of the regeneration process.
source: As the appearances of Pax7 as well as that of centrally located nuclei are accepted markers of muscle regeneration (Lepper et al., 2011; Mazzotti and Coletti, 2016), we concluded that the increased expression of Septin7 could also be an essential component of the regeneration process.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between Septin7 expression and regeneration markers.
